title: Longest Subarray With Equal 0s and 1s
statement: You are given a binary array nums containing only the integers 0 and 1. Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray that holds an equal number of 0s and 1s. If no such subarray exists, return 0. Since you only report the length, no tie-breaking is needed when several subarrays share the maximum length.
hints: A subarray is balanced when its count of 1s minus its count of 0s is zero. What quantity, tracked as you scan, lets you detect that two endpoints enclose such a subarray?

Map 0 to -1 and 1 to +1, then keep a running total. Two indices with the same running total delimit a balanced subarray, so store each prefix total in a hashmap the FIRST time you see it (and pre-seed total 0 at index -1).

Walk the array maintaining running. At index i, if running was seen before at index j, the subarray (j, i] is balanced with length i - j; take the max. Only record running -> i when running is new, so j stays as early as possible and the length stays maximal. The seed {0: -1} handles balanced subarrays that begin at index 0.
